kai (customer): Hey team — noticed a sudden billing jump and a couple of 502s from our bulk-embed job around 10:12am PT. Example req id: req_9a2b7c4e. Batch size = 64. Can someone help repro? :eyes:

jenna (support): Sorry about that. Can you paste the minimal curl or SDK call you used and the exact response headers if you have them?

kai (customer): Here's the curl we used:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-lite-001","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"],"batch_size":64}'
```

We get intermittent 502s and occasionally a header `x-billing-usage: tokens=265432;account=acct_9X`. Full response headers (when successful):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: req_9a2b7c4e
x-billing-usage: tokens=265432;compute_usd=12.34
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```

kai (customer): When 502 happens the body is empty and header `x-request-id: req_9a2b7c4e` is still present.

jenna (support): Thanks. Can you run the same curl with -v and paste stderr (verbose) and also run a tiny SDK reproducer in py/js/go below and paste outputs? This helps us capture timings and header order.

jenna (support): Minimal Python repro (please run from same env):

```
# run with: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
import os, requests
url = "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings"
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-lite-001","input":["a","b","c"],"batch_size":64}
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}","Content-Type":"application/json"}
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(r.status_code)
print(r.headers)
print(r.text[:1000])
```

jenna (support): Minimal Node.js repro:

```
// run with: REDWOOD_API_KEY=... node repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings',{
    method:'POST',
    headers:{ 'Authorization':`Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type':'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model:'text-embedding-lite-001', input:['a','b','c'], batch_size:64 })
  })
  console.log(res.status)
  console.log(Object.fromEntries(res.headers))
  console.log(await res.text())
})()
```

jenna (support): Minimal Go repro:

```
// run with: REDWOOD_API_KEY=... go run repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main(){
  b := []byte(`{"model":"text-embedding-lite-001","input":["a","b","c"],"batch_size":64}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewReader(b))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil { fmt.Println("err:",err); return }
  fmt.Println("status",resp.StatusCode)
  for k,v := range resp.Header { fmt.Println(k,":",v) }
}
```

mike (eng): Also double-check you're not hitting a quota/billing plan change at the account level. Can you paste the account id (acct_9X masked ok) and whether you toggled model or region recently? I suspect an internal spike on batch path. :thinking:

kai (customer): Account is acct_9X (masked). No model or region change. We did increase batch size from 32 -> 64 yesterday.
